topics.title: Family and Fun: Playing Together with Bela
topics.concept_summary: Namaste Vihana! Come, let us step into the cheerful world of our friend Bela! Bela lives with her wonderful brothers—Banku Bhaiya, her older brother, and sweet little Bishu. Have you ever wondered why playing together makes brothers, sisters, and friends feel so close? When Bela and her brothers play 'chhupan-chhupai'—which is the Hindi name for hide-and-seek—they learn to take turns, look out for one another, and share joyful giggles. A family is like a little team where everyone cares for each other, whether during study time or playful outdoor games. Isn't that lovely, Vihana?

topics.title: What is a Community? Helping Hands Together
topics.concept_summary: Now, Vihana, let's look beyond Bela's front door to all the houses nearby! Many different families live close to one another, and together they form what we call a 'community'. But why do we live in communities instead of living all alone in the woods? We live together because of 'mutual aid', which means helping each other out whenever someone is in need. When neighbors share tools, help fix a fence, or clean the street together, that collective effort creates a peaceful, harmonious neighborhood. When we cooperate, difficult jobs become light and easy for everyone!

topics.title: Caring for Nature: Plants, Animals, and the Elements
topics.concept_summary: Vihana, did you know that our community includes more than just humans? Yes, our animal friends and green plants are part of our shared home too! Communities cultivate crops and look after farm animals because they generously provide us with delicious food, cozy clothing, and clean air. We also show deep respect and gratitude to natural elements like the bright sun, glowing moon, fresh air, cool water, and rich soil. When we protect our environment, we are thanking Mother Nature for giving us everything we need to stay healthy and strong. Isn't that a wonderful duty to have?

topics.title: Celebrations and Melas: Joy Brings Us Together
topics.concept_summary: Put on your festive clothes, Vihana, because it is time to celebrate! In our communities, we gather for wonderful festivals and vibrant village fairs called 'melas'. Why do we celebrate together instead of just partying at home? When everyone comes out to the mela to sing folk songs, dance to the beat of the dholak, and play fun games, all differences melt away! Melas remind us that we belong to one big, joyous family under the sky. Sharing happiness multiplies it, making our bond with our neighbors stronger and sweeter than a warm jalebi!

Unit 1 : Our Families and Communities

We all come from different families that live close to one another in supportive and cooperative communities. Together, we cultivate a variety of plants and care for different animals, contributing to the well-being of our shared environment. 

Through mutual aid and collective efforts, we build vibrant and harmonious communities.This unit explores the many facets of our 
families and communities, highlighting our collaborative work and mutual support. We are dedicated to maintaining and respecting our surroundings, protecting the plants and animals that sustain us with food, clothing, 
and more. Celebrations, such as melas and festivals, bring us together 
to play, sing, and dance, while we also express gratitude by respecting 
the natural elements including the sun, moon, air, water, and soil.

topics.title: The Sun and the Inner Rocky Planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars)
topics.concept_summary: Namaste Student! Today, we are going on a magical journey through space to explore 'Our Solar System'. At the very center of our cosmic neighborhood is the Sun, which is a giant, magnificent star made of blazing hot gas. It acts like the king of the house, holding everything together with an invisible superpower called gravity while giving us light and warmth. Close to the Sun are the first four planets—Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars—which are made of hard rock, just like the stones we walk on here on Earth. Mercury is closest and feels like a fiery oven by day and an ice cube by night, while Venus is the hottest of all because its thick clouds trap the heat. Then comes our very own Earth, our beautiful blue home filled with fresh air and oceans, followed by Mars, the Red Planet with rusty soil and the biggest volcano in space!

topics.title: The Asteroid Belt and the Giant Outer Planets (Jupiter and Saturn)
topics.concept_summary: Let's travel further out into space, Student! After we pass the rocky planets, we cross a busy highway of floating space rocks called the Asteroid Belt, which sits right between Mars and Jupiter. Once we cross this belt, we enter the kingdom of the colossal gas giants! Jupiter is the biggest giant of them all, sporting a famous swirling storm called the Great Red Spot that is so huge it could swallow Earth whole. Right next door is Saturn, the absolute jewel of space, famous for wearing a dazzling crown of bright rings made of billions of ice chunks and space dust. Isn't that just breathtaking to imagine?

topics.title: The Chilly Ice Giants (Uranus, Neptune) and the Outer Edges
topics.concept_summary: We are reaching the very edge of our solar system now! Here in the deep freeze live the chilly ice giants: Uranus and Neptune. Uranus is a very quirky planet because it doesn't spin upright like a spinning top; instead, it rolls around on its side like a rolling barrel! Farther out is Neptune, a brilliant deep blue world where the wildest, fastest winds in the solar system sweep across its surface. And if we go even further beyond Neptune, we find the mysterious Kuiper Belt, which is home to icy comets and tiny dwarf planets like Pluto. Isn't our solar system full of wonderful surprises?

curr_solar_system.full_pdf_text:
Our Solar System is a cosmic neighborhood consisting of the Sun and eight wonderful planets orbiting around it, held together by the invisible pull of gravity.
At the center is our Sun, a magnificent star of blazing hot gas that provides light, warmth, and energy to everything around it.
The four inner planets closest to the Sun are small, rocky worlds: Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars.
Mercury is the closest to the Sun and has extreme temperatures with boiling hot days and freezing cold nights.
Venus is the hottest planet, covered in thick swirling yellow clouds that trap heat like a giant oven.
Earth is our beautiful blue home planet, the only known place with liquid oceans, fresh air with oxygen, and living creatures.
Mars is called the Red Planet because its soil contains iron oxide rust, and it has the tallest volcano in the solar system named Olympus Mons.
Between Mars and Jupiter is the Asteroid Belt, where thousands of rocky space boulders orbit the Sun.
Next come the outer planets, which are colossal giants!
Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system, with a famous swirling storm called the Great Red Spot that is bigger than Earth.
Saturn is the jewel of space, adorned with dazzling rings made of billions of ice chunks and space dust.
Uranus is a chilly ice giant that uniquely spins on its side like a rolling barrel.
Neptune is the farthest planet, a brilliant deep blue world swept by the fastest, wildest winds in the solar system.
Beyond Neptune lies the Kuiper Belt, home to icy comets and dwarf planets like Pluto.

curr_de1dcd0ffd.full_pdf_text:
The Inspiring Life of Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam was born on 15 October 1931 in Rameswaram, a small
town in Tamil Nadu, India. He grew up in a humble family and learned the values
of hard work, honesty, and kindness from his parents. As a child, he helped his
family by distributing newspapers while continuing his studies with great
determination. His love for learning and science led him to become an aerospace
scientist, and he played an important role in India’s space and missile
development programmes. Because of his contributions, he became widely
known as the “Missile Man of India.” In 2002, he became the 11th President of
India, serving the country with humility and inspiring millions of young people to
dream big, work hard, and use their knowledge to help others. Even after his
presidency, he continued to teach and encourage students. Dr. Kalam passed
away on 27 July 2015 while delivering a lecture to students, doing what he loved
most. His life reminds us that great achievements can begin with simple dreams,
sincere effort, and a strong desire to serve our nation.

curr_b39c1c8b9b.full_pdf_text:
The Solar System
1. The Solar System is made up of the Sun and all the objects that orbit it.
2. The Sun is a star at the center of the Solar System.
3. Its gravity keeps the planets moving around it.
4. There are eight planets in the Solar System.
5. Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun.
6. Venus is the hottest planet because of its thick atmosphere.
7. Earth is our home and the only planet known to support life.
8. Mars is called the Red Planet because of its reddish surface.
9. Jupiter is the largest planet in the Solar System.
10. Saturn is famous for its beautiful rings.
11. Uranus rotates on its side compared with most planets.
12. Neptune is the farthest planet from the Sun.
13. Planets travel around the Sun in paths called orbits.
14. The Moon is Earth's natural satellite.
15. Some planets have many moons, while others have few or none.
16. Asteroids are rocky objects that orbit the Sun.
17. Comets are made mostly of ice, dust, and rock.
18. The Solar System also contains dwarf planets, such as Pluto.
19. Light from the Sun takes about eight minutes to reach Earth.
20. Studying the Solar System helps us understand space and our place in it.
